entries.1063fdea99ce8307: It generates power at hydroelectric, thermal, wind and other power plants of the company or its affiliates, and also sells electricity procured from wholesale electricity trading markets and other sources. Through its subsidiaries’ transmission and transformation facilities, it provides power wheeling for 9 general transmission and distribution utilities, excluding The Okinawa Electric Power Company, Incorporated, and it operates power generation businesses overseas, such as in Thailand and the United States. Its coal-fired power plants mainly use overseas coal as fuel.
entries.1de3e516ae009147: The group consists of the company, 109 subsidiaries and 86 affiliates (as of March 31, 2026). It designates its 5 [[term:segment|reportable segments]] as the Power Generation Business, Transmission and Transformation Business, Electric Power-Related Business, Overseas Business and Other Businesses. The company was established in September 1952 as a government-invested joint-stock company under the Electric Power Development Promotion Law.

entries.49be029d47d1c7af: In the Power Generation Business, it supplies electricity under contracts that set output, electricity volume, rates and other terms with retail electricity businesses such as the 10 former general electricity utilities and new power companies. Most of its operating revenue is described as rate income from sales in Japan to the former general electricity utilities. The main customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were the Japan Electric Power Exchange (general incorporated association), ¥191,732 million; Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand, ¥147,095 million; and The Chugoku Electric Power Co., Inc., ¥121,889 million.

entries.5b04dce81ed01b29: This reportable segment provides power wheeling services through the transmission and substation facilities held by subsidiaries, for nine general transmission and distribution operators excluding The Okinawa Electric Power Company, Inc. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥49,270 million, of which power wheeling revenue was ¥48,847 million. Revenue fell 1.2% from the previous year, due to lower wheeling revenue. As of March 31, 2026, the domestic subsidiaries' transmission facilities had a total route length of 2,410.3 km (2,143.1 km AC and 267.2 km DC), with 5 substations, 1 frequency conversion station and 4 AC-DC conversion facilities. Among the consolidated subsidiaries whose main business is listed as "transmission business" in the related companies section, is Dengen Transmission and Distribution Network Co., Ltd. (ownership of voting rights 100.0%).

entries.62dc01df47d7e164: Net income attributable to owners of the parent for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥58.5 billion, a decrease of ¥33.9 billion (36.7%) from the previous year. The reasons were the recognition of impairment losses on renewable energy power generation facilities in Australia and the Takasago Thermal Power Plant, etc., as well as the recognition of a loss on retirement of noncurrent assets arising from the retirement of some equipment under the Ohma Nuclear Power Plant project. When coal prices rise sharply, a time lag before fuel cost increases are reflected in rates can temporarily hurt business performance.
entries.697e2428095273f3: Under its long-term vision toward 2050, “BLUE MISSION 2050,” it aims to achieve carbon neutrality in the Power Generation Business and, to accelerate efforts from 2030 onward, to transform its business portfolio in Japan and overseas, centered on carbon-neutral assets. The key priorities of the Medium-Term Management Plan (2024–2026) are establishing and growing sustainable revenue sources (domestic renewable energy business and Overseas Business); laying the groundwork for the business portfolio of the 2030s (CO2-free hydrogen and ammonia strategy, contributing to strengthening power networks, promoting the Ohma Nuclear Power Plant project, and creating new business domains); improving profitability and investment efficiency; strengthening group competitiveness; and deepening ESG management. As a non-financial target, it aims to reduce CO2 emissions from domestic power generation by 22.5 million t (46%) by 2030 compared with fiscal 2013.
entries.734e67d7c2ba145e: This reportable segment covers power generation by the company or its affiliates, including hydroelectric, thermal and wind power, along with their maintenance and operation, and the sale of electricity procured from the wholesale electricity trading market and other sources. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥840,445 million, the largest of the five reportable segments. Electricity sold in the same fiscal year was 66.7 billion kWh, down 1.7% from the previous year. This comprised 9.8 billion kWh from renewable energy, 41.8 billion kWh from thermal power, and 15 billion kWh of electricity procured from the wholesale electricity trading market and other sources. Revenue including intersegment internal revenue fell 10.5% from the previous year, due to the decommissioning of the Matsushima Thermal Power Station and a decline in capacity market prices. As of March 31, 2026, the company's facilities comprised 61 hydroelectric power stations, 7 steam power stations, and 2 power stations for new energy and other sources. Major customers are the Japan Electric Power Exchange (revenue ¥191,732 million) and The Chugoku Electric Power Co., Inc. (revenue ¥121,889 million).

entries.e1fbb7d57b5b786a: Revenue (operating revenue) for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,182.2 billion, a decrease of ¥134.4 billion (10.2%) from the previous year. The reasons were a decrease in electricity sales volume in Thailand, the decommissioning and suspension of the Matsushima Thermal Power Plant, and lower capacity market prices. Since the abolition of wholesale regulations, etc. in April 2016, sales rates for the domestic Power Generation Business have been determined through negotiation with customers. Sales rates to the wholesale electricity trading market are based on electricity market prices, and the portion of thermal power costs corresponding to fuel costs reflects market fluctuations. Transmission business rates are calculated by adding reasonable profit to reasonable costs.

entries.fc86531b8ab16c82: This reportable segment covers power generation overseas and related businesses. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥227,896 million, the second largest of the reportable segments. Its revenue mainly consists of electricity sales under long-term power sales agreements between a consolidated subsidiary and the Electricity Generating Public Company Limited (EGAT) in Thailand, and electricity sales in the electricity market by a consolidated subsidiary in the United States. Electricity sold in the same fiscal year fell 19.5% from the previous year to 14.4 billion kWh, due to lower sales in Thailand, and revenue fell 6.9% from the previous year. As of March 31, 2026, the segment had 14 power stations, including gas-fired thermal power facilities, solar power facilities and storage battery facilities. Major customer is the Electricity Generating Public Company Limited (EGAT) (revenue ¥147,095 million).
